## Structural Validation of Novel Calls {#structural-validation-of-novel-calls}

Novel transcripts are candidates, not findings. This section reports the structural evidence gathered for each one, and nothing here filters the output: every transcript counted above is still present. The point is to say which candidates carry warning signs and which do not, so that a count is never quoted without knowing what sits behind it.

Evidence is reported separately for the three categories a novel model is routed into — **novel lncRNA candidates**, models **predicted protein-coding**, and models **predicted non-coding** — because the same warning sign does not carry the same weight in each.

Strand relative to the reference gene is carried by the classification itself. For every candidate class code except `i` it is fixed: `x` is antisense by definition, and `j`, `k`, `o`, `y`, `m` and `n` are same-strand matches. Class code `i` is reported as **sense intronic** or **antisense intronic**, and that distinction is what the figures below are grouped on.

The read-level test asks whether the reads supporting a candidate stop where the candidate stops. Reads running past its boundaries, or carrying splice junctions that belong to the host rather than to the candidate, came from a longer molecule — most often the host's own **unspliced precursor**, the primary transcript before its introns are removed. A sense-intronic candidate is sequence-identical to part of that precursor, so position alone cannot separate the two; an antisense candidate cannot be explained that way at all. Hosts are frequently lncRNA genes rather than protein-coding ones — a lncRNA gene is transcribed by Pol II and spliced just as a protein-coding gene is — so the host biotype is reported alongside every candidate.

```{r}
#| label: context-prep
#| echo: false

read_csv_safe <- function(path) {
  if (is.null(path) || !file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  df <- tryCatch(read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(df) || !nrow(df)) NULL else df
}

ctx_flags   <- read_csv_safe(params$context_flags)
ctx_summary <- read_csv_safe(params$context_summary)
novel_nc    <- read_csv_safe(params$novel_non_coding_meta)

#' Attach the routed category and the classification wording to a table keyed on
#' qry_id. Anything the metadata does not carry is named rather than dropped.
#'
#' The classification, not the bare class code, is what the figures in this section
#' group on: it carries the sense/antisense split of `i`, which is the only strand
#' distinction that varies within a class code.
add_novel_category <- function(df, id_col = "qry_id") {
  if (is.null(df) || !nrow(df)) return(df)

  df$novel_category <- NA_character_
  df$classification <- NA_character_

  if (exists("novel_tx") && "transcript_biotype" %in% names(novel_tx)) {
    idx <- match(df[[id_col]], novel_tx$qry_id)
    df$novel_category <- unname(NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS[novel_tx$transcript_biotype[idx]])
    if ("classification" %in% names(novel_tx)) {
      df$classification <- novel_tx$classification[idx]
    }
  }

  df$novel_category[is.na(df$novel_category)] <- "not routed"
  miss <- is.na(df$classification) | !nzchar(df$classification)
  df$classification[miss] <- ifelse(is.na(df$class_code[miss]), "unknown",
                                    df$class_code[miss])

  df$novel_category <- factor(df$novel_category,
                              levels = c(unname(NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS), "not routed"))
  df
}

ctx_flags <- add_novel_category(ctx_flags)

# Chunk options cannot use `!expr !is.null(x)`: YAML reads `!expr` as a tag and
# then hits a second `!`, which is a duplicate tag property and a parse error.
# Same reason the existing scaffold chunks carry a plain `has_*` flag.
has_ctx_flags <- !is.null(ctx_flags)

ctx_metric <- function(key) {
  if (is.null(ctx_summary)) return(NA_integer_)
  v <- ctx_summary$value[ctx_summary$metric == key]
  if (length(v)) as.integer(v[1]) else NA_integer_
}

fmt_n <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) "not recorded" else format(x, big.mark = ",")
```

```{r}
#| label: context-callout
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if (is.null(ctx_flags)) {
  cat('::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}\n')
  cat("## Structural validation did not run\n\n")
  cat("No `novel_context_flags.csv` was available, so the candidates in this report ")
  cat("carry no structural evidence. Every count above should be read as unvalidated.\n")
  cat(":::\n")
} else {
  same  <- ctx_metric("same_strand_as_host")
  opp   <- ctx_metric("opposite_strand_to_host")
  isame <- ctx_metric("intronic_same_strand")
  ijunc <- ctx_metric("intronic_same_strand_with_host_junction")
  none  <- ctx_metric("no_reads_recovered")

  cat('::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}\n')
  cat("## Structural evidence, in short\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("- **%s** candidates evaluated.\n", fmt_n(ctx_metric("candidates_evaluated"))))
  cat(sprintf("- **%s** lie within a host gene: %s on the same strand, %s on the opposite strand.\n",
              fmt_n(ctx_metric("with_host_gene")), fmt_n(same), fmt_n(opp)))
  cat(sprintf("- **%s** are intronic *and* on the host's strand, which is the ambiguous population.\n",
              fmt_n(isame)))
  cat(sprintf("- Of those, **%s** are supported by reads carrying one of the host's splice junctions, which is evidence those reads came from the host.\n",
              fmt_n(ijunc)))
  if (!is.na(none) && none > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("- **%s** recovered no overlapping reads at all and cannot be assessed either way.\n",
                fmt_n(none)))
  }
  cat("\n:::\n")
}
```

### Read-level evidence

```{r}
#| label: fig-context-reads
#| fig-cap: "**Fraction of supporting reads that run past a transcript's boundaries, and fraction carrying one of the host gene's splice junctions, split by routed category.** A discrete transcript sits near zero on both. Values near one mean the reads supporting the call belong to a longer molecule, most likely the host's unspliced precursor. The x axis is the classification, which separates sense- from antisense-intronic candidates: only the sense-intronic ones can be confused with the host's own precursor. Only transcripts with a reference gene and at least one recovered read are shown."
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 9
#| eval: !expr has_ctx_flags

reads_df <- ctx_flags %>%
  filter(!is.na(same_strand_as_host), reads_total > 0) %>%
  select(novel_category, classification,
         frac_crossing_boundary, frac_with_host_junction) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(frac_crossing_boundary, frac_with_host_junction),
               names_to = "measure", values_to = "fraction") %>%
  mutate(measure = recode(measure,
    frac_crossing_boundary  = "reads crossing a boundary",
    frac_with_host_junction = "reads carrying a host junction")) %>%
  droplevels()

ggplot(reads_df, aes(x = classification, y = fraction, fill = measure)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  # One row per routed category, free x because the class codes reaching each are
  # different by construction -- a shared axis would reserve empty slots in every
  # panel for codes that cannot appear in it.
  facet_wrap(~novel_category, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "viridis", begin = 0.25, end = 0.75) +
  theme_width(13) +
  labs(title = "Read-level evidence against each novel transcript",
       subtitle = "Higher is worse: the supporting reads do not stop where the transcript does",
       x = NULL, y = "Fraction of supporting reads", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        strip.text  = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

### Which warning signs occur together

The figures above each show one signal at a time. What decides whether a candidate is worth distrusting is whether the signals **agree** — and that is a question about combinations, not about any single distribution.

Each bar below is one exact combination of flags. The transcripts to look at first are in the bar carrying the most flags at once: intronic, on the host's strand, unspliced, supported by reads that run past its boundaries and carry the host's junctions. That is the profile of a precursor fragment, and it is one bar you can point at rather than a conjunction you have to assemble from five figures.

Every flag here is structural and threshold-free — each is a count being zero or non-zero, not a value crossing a cutoff.

```{r}
#| label: evidence-sets-prep
#| include: false

evidence_sets <- NULL

if (!is.null(ctx_flags)) {
  ev <- ctx_flags
  if (exists("novel_tx") && "exon" %in% names(novel_tx)) {
    ev <- dplyr::left_join(ev, novel_tx[, c("qry_id", "exon")], by = "qry_id")
  } else {
    ev$exon <- NA_character_
  }

  # Full-length support is membership of Bambu's fullLengthCounts matrix, which is
  # a zero/non-zero fact rather than a threshold on a fraction.
  fl_ids <- if (exists("bambu_ids") && !is.null(bambu_ids$fullLength)) {
    bambu_ids$fullLength
  } else {
    character(0)
  }

  # Strand is not a set here. It varies only for class code i, and that variation is
  # carried by the classification -- sense intronic against antisense intronic --
  # which is the fill. As a set it would spend a matrix row restating the colour.
  evidence_sets <- ev %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      `mono-exonic`                 = !is.na(exon) & exon == "mono-exonic",
      `reads cross a boundary`      = reads_crossing_boundary > 0,
      `reads carry a host junction` = reads_with_host_junction > 0,
      `no full-length support`      = !(qry_id %in% fl_ids),
      classification                = factor(classification)
    )

  if (!nrow(evidence_sets)) evidence_sets <- NULL
}

has_evidence_sets <- !is.null(evidence_sets)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-evidence-upset
#| fig-cap: "**Combinations of structural warning signs, one figure per routed category.** Each bar is one exact combination; the dot matrix below names it. Bars are stacked by classification, which is mutually exclusive and therefore a fill rather than a set. Set sizes are in the row labels, and a candidate in the leftmost bar carries no warning signs at all."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| eval: !expr has_evidence_sets

# One UpSet per routed category. The same combination of flags does not carry the
# same weight in each: boundary read-through on a predicted protein-coding model
# suggests a truncated mRNA, where on a sense-intronic lncRNA candidate it is the
# signature of the host's own precursor.
for (cat_name in levels(droplevels(evidence_sets$novel_category))) {
  sub <- evidence_sets[evidence_sets$novel_category == cat_name, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(sub)) next

  p <- plot_upset(
    droplevels(sub),
    sets = c("mono-exonic", "reads cross a boundary",
             "reads carry a host junction", "no full-length support"),
    fill_col = "classification",
    title    = sprintf("Structural warning signs: %s", cat_name),
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "%s candidates; more flags at once means less of the evidence is explained by a real, discrete transcript",
      format(nrow(sub), big.mark = ",")),
    empty_label = "no warning signs")

  if (!is.null(p)) print(p)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: evidence-upset-note
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if (!is.null(evidence_sets)) {
  n_all <- sum(evidence_sets$`same strand as host` &
               evidence_sets$`reads cross a boundary` &
               evidence_sets$`reads carry a host junction`, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_clean <- sum(!evidence_sets$`same strand as host` &
                 !evidence_sets$`reads cross a boundary` &
                 !evidence_sets$`reads carry a host junction`, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "Of %s candidates, **%s** carry all three host-relationship flags at once ",
    "(same strand, boundary read-through, host junctions), and **%s** carry none ",
    "of them. Neither number is a verdict: the first is the set to inspect, the ",
    "second is the set with nothing arguing against it.\n"),
    format(nrow(evidence_sets), big.mark = ","),
    format(n_all, big.mark = ","),
    format(n_clean, big.mark = ",")))
}
```

### Full-length and uniquely-mapped support

Bambu reports, per transcript, how many reads support it in total, how many span its full structure, and how many map to it uniquely. Read alongside the class code, these separate a transcript that reads *fit* from one that reads merely *overlap*.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Read the low tail, not the high one

A novel model's boundaries were placed **by** the reads now being counted against it. A read that spans the model end to end is, in large part, a read that decided where those ends go — so a high full-length fraction restates how the model was built rather than testing it, and confirms nothing.

The informative direction is the **low** tail: a candidate whose supporting reads mostly fail to span it is a fragment of something longer. Treat this as a screen that points at transcripts worth inspecting, not as a verdict on any of them.
:::

```{r}
#| label: support-prep
#| echo: false

# Per-transcript totals across all samples. The first column is the transcript id
# and every numeric column after it is one sample.
read_support <- function(path, label) {
  df <- tryCatch(read.delim(path, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(df) || !nrow(df)) return(NULL)
  num <- df[, vapply(df, is.numeric, logical(1)), drop = FALSE]
  if (!ncol(num)) return(NULL)
  out <- data.frame(transcript_id = as.character(df[[1]]),
                    value = rowSums(num, na.rm = TRUE),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(out)[2] <- label
  out
}

sup_total <- read_support(params$counts_transcript,    "reads_total")
sup_full  <- read_support(params$fl_counts_transcript, "reads_full_length")
sup_uniq  <- read_support(params$u_counts_transcript,  "reads_unique")

support <- NULL
if (!is.null(sup_total) && !is.null(sup_full) && !is.null(sup_uniq)) {
  support <- sup_total %>%
    inner_join(sup_full, by = "transcript_id") %>%
    inner_join(sup_uniq, by = "transcript_id") %>%
    inner_join(novel_tx[, c("qry_id", "class_code", "biotype", "classification",
                            "exon")],
               by = c("transcript_id" = "qry_id")) %>%
    filter(reads_total > 0) %>%
    mutate(full_length_fraction = reads_full_length / reads_total,
           unique_fraction      = reads_unique      / reads_total,
           # `biotype` already holds the routed category's display label, so the
           # split here uses the same names as every other figure in this section.
           novel_category = factor(biotype,
                                   levels = c(unname(NOVEL_BIOTYPE_LABELS),
                                              "novel (unclassified)")))
  if (!nrow(support)) support <- NULL
}

has_support <- !is.null(support)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-support-fraction
#| fig-cap: "**Full-length and uniquely-mapped read support for novel transcripts, split by routed category.** Columns are the two support measures, rows the three categories, and the x axis the classification. Low full-length support means the reads behind a call do not span it; low unique support means those reads are compatible with other transcripts too, so the count came largely from expectation-maximisation rather than from unambiguous evidence."
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 10
#| eval: !expr has_support

support_long <- support %>%
  select(novel_category, classification, exon,
         full_length_fraction, unique_fraction) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(full_length_fraction, unique_fraction),
               names_to = "measure", values_to = "fraction") %>%
  mutate(measure = recode(measure,
    full_length_fraction = "full-length / total",
    unique_fraction      = "uniquely mapped / total")) %>%
  droplevels()

# theme_width() returns a complete theme, which replaces everything set before it,
# so it goes first and the specific tweaks follow.
ggplot(support_long, aes(x = classification, y = fraction, fill = exon)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(novel_category), cols = vars(measure), scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "viridis", begin = 0.3, end = 0.8) +
  theme_width(13) +
  labs(title = "Read support for novel transcripts",
       subtitle = "Low values mark candidates whose supporting reads fit them poorly",
       x = NULL, y = "Fraction of supporting reads", fill = "Exon class") +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        strip.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", angle = 0),
        strip.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-support-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Median read support by novel transcript category and class code."
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr has_support

support %>%
  group_by(biotype, class_code) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `median full-length` = sprintf("%.2f", median(full_length_fraction)),
            `median unique`      = sprintf("%.2f", median(unique_fraction)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(biotype, class_code) %>%
  knitr::kable(format = "markdown")
```

### What the predicted non-coding category holds

```{r}
#| label: non-coding-note
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

if (is.null(novel_nc)) {
  cat("No models were routed to the predicted non-coding category in this run.\n")
} else {
  by_class <- sort(table(novel_nc$classification), decreasing = TRUE)
  class_txt <- paste(sprintf("%s (%d)", names(by_class), as.integer(by_class)),
                     collapse = ", ")

  hosts <- sort(table(novel_nc$ref_gene_biotype, useNA = "ifany"), decreasing = TRUE)
  host_names <- names(hosts)
  host_names[is.na(host_names)] <- "no reference gene"
  host_txt <- paste(sprintf("%s (%d)", host_names, as.integer(hosts)), collapse = ", ")

  cat('::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}\n')
  cat("## Composition of this category\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("**%s** models are predicted non-coding and share splice structure with a reference gene that is not an lncRNA.\n\n",
              format(nrow(novel_nc), big.mark = ",")))
  cat(sprintf("By classification: %s.\n\n", class_txt))
  cat(sprintf("By reference gene biotype: %s.\n\n", host_txt))
  cat("Each of these has no detected coding potential while belonging structurally to a locus that is not a non-coding gene. That combination is consistent with an unproductive isoform of the reference gene, and it is also consistent with a genuine non-coding transcript at a shared locus. The category names what is known without choosing between them; the full table is in `novel_non_coding_metadata.csv`.\n")
  cat("\n:::\n")
}
```

## Genomic Context

Coverage and transcript models drawn together at selected loci. The bigWig tracks behind these figures are published alongside the report, so any region can be opened in IGV to explore beyond the windows chosen here.

```{r}
#| label: genomic-context-prep
#| echo: false

gc_clean   <- read_csv_safe(params$genomic_context_candidates)
gc_flagged <- read_csv_safe(params$intronic_context_candidates)

# A figure is embedded only when its PNG was actually staged, so a stub run or a
# partially failed draw leaves a gap rather than a broken image.
embed_figures <- function(df, file_col, tab_col, caption_fn) {
  # tab_col may name several candidates; the first one present is used. A tab still
  # needs a label when the candidates table predates the preferred column.
  tab_col <- if (is.null(df)) NA_character_ else {
    hit <- tab_col[tab_col %in% names(df)]
    if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_character_
  }
  if (is.null(df) || !(file_col %in% names(df)) || is.na(tab_col)) {
    cat("No figures were produced for this section.\n\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  present <- df[!is.na(df[[file_col]]) & file.exists(df[[file_col]]), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(present)) {
    cat("No figures were produced for this section.\n\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(present))) {
    cat(sprintf("## %s\n\n", present[[tab_col]][i]))
    cat(sprintf("![%s](%s)\n\n", caption_fn(present[i, ]), present[[file_col]][i]))
  }
  cat(":::\n\n")
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

### One example per kind of novel call

These panels are chosen to span the ways a novel model can relate to the annotation. A stratum is the combination of routed category, classification and reference gene class — a sense-intronic lncRNA candidate inside a protein-coding gene is a different claim from the same model inside an lncRNA gene, and each gets its own panel. Within a stratum the richest locus is chosen, so every panel is the most informative example of its kind.

Class code `u` is not represented: it is intergenic, so there is no reference gene to draw it against.

Each panel shows the reference gene's full exonic footprint, then every isoform at the locus with novel ones coloured by biotype, then one coverage track per sample on a shared scale.

```{r}
#| label: fig-genomic-context-clean
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

embed_figures(gc_clean, "figure", c("stratum", "label"), function(r) {
  ref_bt <- if (is.null(r$ref_gene_biotype) || is.na(r$ref_gene_biotype) ||
                !nzchar(as.character(r$ref_gene_biotype))) {
    as.character(r$ref_class)
  } else {
    as.character(r$ref_gene_biotype)
  }
  sprintf("%s, %s at %s (%s) — %s:%s-%s. %d isoforms, %d novel. Example: %s.",
          r$novel_biotype, r$classification, r$label, ref_bt,
          r$chrom, format(r$win_s, big.mark = ","),
          format(r$win_e, big.mark = ","), r$n_tx, r$n_novel, r$example_tx)
})
```

### Flagged intronic candidates

These are chosen for the opposite reason: each is an intronic candidate on its host's strand whose supporting reads run past its boundaries or carry the host's splice junctions. They are drawn windowed on the **whole host intron**, because a window drawn tightly around a truncated fragment looks like a discrete transcript whatever it is. The flanking intron is where the difference shows.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## What to look for

A candidate that really is host precursor shows coverage running flat across the entire intron and continuous with the flanking exons. A candidate that is a genuine independent transcript shows a discrete block of coverage with quiet intron either side. If a flagged candidate looks discrete here, the flag is what needs revisiting, not the transcript.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-genomic-context-flagged
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

embed_figures(gc_flagged, "figure", "qry_id", function(r) {
  host <- ifelse(is.na(r$ref_gene_name) | !nzchar(r$ref_gene_name),
                 r$ref_gene_id, r$ref_gene_name)
  pct  <- function(x) if (is.null(x) || !length(x) || is.na(x)) NA_real_ else 100 * x
  fc   <- pct(r$frac_crossing)
  fj   <- pct(r$frac_host_junction)
  fe   <- pct(r$frac_into_host_exon)

  # Fractions, not counts, and for the same reason the selection ranks on fractions:
  # a raw count of host-junction reads ranks by expression. Falls back to counts for
  # a candidates table written before those columns existed.
  ev <- if (is.na(fc) || is.na(fj)) {
    sprintf("%d reads: %d cross a boundary, %d carry a host junction",
            r$reads_total, r$reads_crossing_boundary, r$reads_with_host_junction)
  } else {
    sprintf("%d reads: %.0f%% cross a boundary, %.0f%% carry a host junction%s",
            r$reads_total, fc, fj,
            if (is.na(fe)) "" else
              sprintf(", %.0f%% splice into a host exon", fe))
  }
  sprintf("%s inside an intron of %s (%s). %s.", r$qry_id, host,
          r$ref_gene_biotype, ev)
})
```
